adjudication_notes: Mathematical content is standard algebraic geometry (étale ⇔ smooth-preserving); the obstruction is valid and load-bearing for the C66-GEO-Z → C66-GEO-COMP → C66-TATE-SUPPORT chain. Evidence class retained as adversarial_review rather than upgraded to primary_source because the live-web evidence stage was bounded/unavailable and no workspace source directly asserts or denies smoothness of the reduced-support open for the genus-6 balanced tetragonal family. Retain as candidate pending an independent primary-source verification of (i) local freeness of π_*(W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{-1}) over the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz space and (ii) smoothness of the reduced-support open in the resulting relative linear system; upon such verification the finding should be promoted to corroborated.
contradiction_resolution: No contradiction with any cross-checked claim (CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, RED-0001). Compatible with and complementary to corroborated sibling findings FND-0046 (scheme-structure comparison for Abel–Jacobi incidence), FND-0047 (relative linear system identification requires cohomology-and-base-change when h^0 jumps), FND-0052 (reduced-support locus is open, not closed, so Gysin requires closed stratified embedding), and FND-0058 (constant h^0=3 on the balanced locus is not established). The finding correctly records that finite étale morphisms preserve smoothness in both directions (standard: EGA IV / Stacks Project), so smoothness of Z^{ord,red} is equivalent to smoothness of the reduced-support open in the relative linear system, which is an independent load-bearing geometric claim not discharged by the packet's current C66-GEO-Z / C66-GEO-COMP subproblems. Distinct from FND-0053 (S_6 rational irreps do not force Tate local systems) and FND-0054 (rationality of Hurwitz space is a prediction, not a theorem): do not merge.

scope.mathematical_content: A finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in the relative linear system |W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{-1}| is smooth if and only if that open (and the ambient relative linear system) is itself smooth. Smoothness of the base requires local freeness of π_*(W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{-1}) (cohomology-and-base-change) and a smoothness criterion for the incidence of six distinct points; neither is discharged in the packet.
scope.object: ordered distinct six-point failure locus Z^{ord,red} as a stack over the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz space

source_records.note: SRC-0004 (Canning–Larson) supplies Lemma 10.6 degree calculation used by the packet; does not itself assert smoothness of the ordered reduced-support locus. Live-web stage was unavailable; no additional primary source for the smoothness criterion was retrieved in this audit.
